question: Which of the following best describes a progressive tax system?

options.text: Tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases
Uniform tax rate for all income groups
Tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases
Higher tax rate for corporations than individuals

solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A progressive tax system is one where the tax rate increases as the taxable income or amount increases.
 
• This system is designed to impose a higher tax burden on individuals or entities with higher incomes, ensuring equitable distribution of wealth.
 
• It is commonly used in many countries to reduce income inequality and provide funds for public services.
 
• Examples of progressive taxes include income tax brackets, where higher income levels are taxed at higher rates.
 
• The principle of "ability to pay" is central to progressive taxation, meaning those with greater financial resources contribute more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regressive Tax:** A tax system where the tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases, disproportionately affecting lower-income earners.
 
• **Proportional Tax:** Also known as a flat tax, it applies the same tax rate to all income levels, regardless of the amount earned.
 
• **Examples of Progressive Tax:** U.S. Federal Income Tax, where tax brackets increase with higher income levels.
 
• **Tax Brackets:** Income ranges defined by law where specific tax rates apply, forming the foundation of progressive taxation.
 
• **Redistribution of Wealth:** Progressive taxation aims to reduce economic disparities by transferring resources from higher-income earners to fund programs for the broader population.
